title: Dependency failure scavenger and SLA signal fabric
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a cross-service failure scavenger that automatically identifies dependency-induced failures (downstream timeouts, overloaded upstreams, gRPC/HTTP error codes, and model rejection signals), enriches traces and logs, and surfaces correlated SLA exposure on a new ‘Dependency Signal Fabric’ dashboard.
background: We currently have high-level error dashboards that surface runtime and model faults but lack a reliable way to tie downstream dependency failures (e.g., model-serving pool OOMs, third-party vector DB timeouts, region network issues) to customer-visible SLA exposure. Pager noise and oncall context-switching are high when failures cascade across services. This initiative aims to close the observability gap by adding tracehook enrichment, a lightweight scavenger job, and dashboards that map failure slices to SLO impact.
goals: 1) Instrument tracehooks to attach dependency annotations (dep_type, dep_host, observed_code, retry_count, svc_backpressure_hint). 2) Build a scavenger pipeline that runs periodic joins across traces, metrics, and logs to surface cross-cutting failure vectors. 3) Create an interactive dashboard that links a failure slice to representative traces, recent deploys, and SLO delta.
success_metrics: - Median time-to-root-cause for dependency-related incidents reduced from 32m to <15m. - Oncall incidents attributed to unknown downstream causes reduced by 40%. - Dashboard adoption: 5+ active teams using the Dependency Signal Fabric within 8 weeks.
acceptance_criteria: Tracehook added to runtime with dependency annotation schema and backwards-compatible default tags
Scavenger job produces a daily failure index table with top-5 dependency contributors and example trace IDs
Dashboard shows SLO exposure per failure vector and links to 3 representative traces and the implicated deploys
Runbook updated with playbook steps to distinguish model rejections vs. overloaded upstreams
Automated tests and CI check to ensure tracehook tagging does not exceed 50 bytes per request

progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff sync with runtime, telemetry, and SRE. Agreed schema fields: dep_type, dep_role, dep_target, observed_code, latency_ms, retry_count, backpressure_signal.

2025-02-18: Tracehook prototype pushed (internal PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pulls/4389) that tags grpc client spans with observed_code and latency_ms. Initial runtime perf microbench shows +1.2% p50 CPU on service A during synthetic load.
2025-02-24: ETL spec reviewed. Chose BigQuery for daily joins and a compact failure_index table keyed by date, failure_vector_hash, top_trace_ids. Priya started SQL job in sandbox.
2025-03-02: Dashboard wireframe in Figma: added slicer controls and SLO exposure heatmap. UX review provided feedback to add quick links to deploy metadata and recent config changes.

2025-03-05: Integration test added to CI to validate tag schema and that trace size increase < 50 bytes. Scavenger job in staging returns plausible failure vectors; observed frequent 'upstream_connection_refused' during canary run.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: We decided to enrich spans instead of shipping new logs to avoid doubling ingestion costs. Tradeoff: some dependency metadata will be truncated for very large payloads; mitigated with a 50-byte budget for tag strings.

Scavenger will run daily in BQ rather than streaming to reduce compute cost and avoid noisy transient joins. Tradeoff: near-real-time detection is delayed, but important incidents will still be caught via trace alerting in runtime SLO rules.
Backoff hint field will be an enum (NONE, SOFT, HARD) to keep tag size small. Teams can map enums to richer signals in the dashboard hover text.
open_blockers: Runtime: need final signoff from runtime performance team on hook insertion points (meeting scheduled 2025-03-06).
Telemetry: storage quota for additional BQ exports needs approval from Finance to scale daily export retention beyond 14 days.
Dashboard: query performance for joins needs optimization before enabling 90-day lookback.
review_feedback: SRE review (2025-02-25): prefer enums for backpressure signals; avoid freeform messages to control cardinality.
Privacy review (2025-02-27): ensure no PII is included in dependency tags; added explicit scrub rule in tracehook implementation.
Performance review (2025-03-01): requested microbench across three services and a guardrail metric to auto-disable verbose tagging under CPU pressure.
implementation_notes: Tracehook proto: fields as strings with max_length enforcement; add compressed boolean for vendor spans.
Telemetry pipeline: use date_partitioned failure_index table with schema: date, vector_hash, vector_label, count, p50_latency, p95_latency, top_trace_ids[3], implicated_deploys[3].
Dashboard queries: precompute per-vector SLO exposure as token-cost-weighted error-rate to reflect hosting economics.
Alerting: create an alert when a single failure_vector accounts for >20% of SLO-error-budget burn in 30m.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout to 3 internal services for 1 week and monitor trace size/CPU; rollback flag available via feature gate.
Stage scavenger pipeline in staging with sample traces and synthetic dependency failures for verification.
Enable dashboard read-only for platform teams for 2 weeks, gather feedback, then enable team-facing widgets.
Postmortem and runbook canonicalization after first production detection.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for tracehook schema and scrubbing rules.
End-to-end test: synthetic dependency failure generator that produces an 'upstream_timeout' and verifies scavenger picks the vector and dashboard links to traces.
Load test: run canary services under 2x load and assert trace payload increase <2% CPU overhead.
notes_for_oncall: When the scavenger flags a new top failure vector, use the dashboard link to inspect the top_trace_ids, check implicated_deploys, and correlate with recent config changes. If evidence points to model pool OOMs, follow Model Pool troubleshooting runbook before escalating to infra.
post_release_tasks: Collect adoption metrics and CLA by 30 days.
Iterate on tag schema based on actual cardinality; convert any high-cardinality freeform fields into enums.
Consider moving frequent vectors into a streaming detection pipeline if daily delays are problematic.
